utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody in the courtroom, now in Courtroom III. Mr. Vanderpuye, I see you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I am, Mr. President. You can see Mr. McCloskey's not here today as well. I spoke to him this morning, and he's still feeling quite unwell. And I know that yesterday I told you we expected him in today. We expect him in tomorrow. And if there's any redirect to be done with this witness, we'll see where we are at the end of the day. But I may proceed with that. Or if it spills into next week, Mr. McCloskey might.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Welcome back to the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have to remind you again that the affirmation to tell the truth you made at the beginning of your testimony still applies. Mr. Tolimir is continuing his cross-examination. Mr. Tolimir, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. May God's peace reign in this house, and may God's will be done in these proceedings, and not necessarily mine. And I greet all the people present in this courtroom today. I greet Mr. Salapura and wish him a pleasant stay in our midst, and I wish him a safe return to his home.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, yesterday we left it off with some issues that I don't want to pursue today. I would like to continue talking about the document that we saw yesterday at the end of our session, and that document was provided by the Documentation Centre based in Banja Luka. And we spoke about that, but I didn't ask you anything about the victims in Zepa and Srebrenica. Were there any victims in Zepa? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were there casualties among our army as a result of the fire of the enemy army during the armed conflict and after the conflict, when the zone was finally demilitarised? What can you tell us about that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were many. I don't know how many, though. In 1992, there was a large number of casualties. Several dozen men were in our column. I can't tell you what date was that. And that column was bringing food for a communications facility. They were ambushed, and they suffered great losses. After that, there were a lot of onslaughts and attacks against facilities, even one against command facilities, or actually several attacks against the command facility. We suffered losses among foot soldiers and officers at the command post. Those were continuous activities carried out by the forces from Zepa. I can't tell you, after such a long time, when that was. In any way, that was a continuous activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We're --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, Mr. Salapura, like yesterday, I would like to remind you to bear in mind you are using the same language and we need a pause between question and answer and the next question. You're starting to overlap again. Please bear that in mind and be very careful with that. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, I apologise to you for not being able to get documents with the exact data as to how many were killed in Zepa and how many in Srebrenica, since the Trial Chamber decided not to continue talking about the document provided by the Documentation Centre. Did you analyse information, and did you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I have to interrupt you. This is a misstatement. The Chamber didn't stop you at all. The Chamber gave you some advice to focus, in the time you may use during cross-examination, on the events in 1995. The Chamber didn't stop you at all. You may read the transcript of yesterday carefully. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. You advised us to focus on 1995. Let me ask Mr. Salapura.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you -- do you remember that a motorised convoy was ambushed when they were carrying food to Zlovrh? That there were over 40 people killed and over 40 captured; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember. And this is exactly what I was talking about. I told you that I didn't know how many there were. There were several dozen men in the convoy. And you'll remember that I personally went to negotiate about the exchange of bodies, and I personally, with my own hand, loaded those decomposing bodies onto a lorry. Those were the bodies of our soldiers that had been killed. And you know that I was beaten at the time. I carried a white flag in my hand because that was the only way I could establish communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, when it comes to the Main Staff, did the Main Staff ever retaliate against Zepa? Did you and I infiltrate sabotage groups into Zepa? Our job was to work in the enemy territory; however, were we able to work in the enemy territory there, in the territory of the enclave of Zepa, as we were supposed to, because that was our job?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that there was one more attack, or perhaps two, coming out of Zepa. A communications facility in the command sector was attacked on the eve of the negotiations that I was supposed to carry out with them. That's when two officers were killed. Two non-commissioned officers were killed about 15 minutes before I turned up for the negotiations. They were minor skirmishes, but we never infiltrated any groups into the territory of Zepa. At the moment that UNPROFOR forces arrived, I believe that the Ukrainian Battalion was there, and we did not carry out any offensive activities at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember whether the Main Staff ever sent protests or demands to UNPROFOR, asking them to curb the attacks coming out from the demilitarised zone?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that happened very often. You were very heavily involved in that. I personally did not participate in the drafting of those protest notes. You were the one who dealt with that, and there were a lot of those. A few over Zepa and over Srebrenica, it happened all the time, because from Srebrenica, provocations and armed attacks were continuous, and we suffered very many losses as a result of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can D16 be displayed in e-court. I apologise. Thank you, Aleksandar. Line 17 -- line 7.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Apologies by the interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You can see the document, Mr. Salapura. And on line 6, the first words are: "The aggressor, on the 16th of February ..." This is a document issued by Bosnia-Herzegovina, which was issued by the Command of the 2nd Corps, and it was sent to the 28th Division, and it is a warning about what we had done. That's when the 28th Division was called the 8th Operative Group. And we request measures to be taken to raise combat activities. And it says here: "The aggressor, on the 16th of February, 1995, filed a request with UNPROFOR to declare Zepa a non-demilitarised zone, with the following rationale:" And helicopter flights are mentioned and attacks from the demilitarised zone. Let me not go on reading any more. Please, do you know that we tried to do that through UNPROFOR, and in a written form, and through meetings at the airport? Do you know about all that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: You were in charge that activity. You co-ordinated that activity with Colonel Magazin [phoen]. I'm not sure about his name, though. At that level, the level of exchanging information, I know that there were daily protests filed with UNPROFOR and that those protests were dealing both with Srebrenica and Zepa.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know anything about an attack that was launched from Zepa at the Main Staff of the VRS? Did you happen to be there in the Main Staff when they launched a direct attack against the Main Staff? Thank you. And can you remember approximately when that was, in what month and what year?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember; of course I do. We were all in trenches at that time. I was the guards commander at the time. I can't tell you when that was. I can't remember the date. However, as far as I know, there was a direct attack, and there was a somewhat smaller-scale attack in the same sector a bit later.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Mr. Salapura. I would like to call up D145.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You will tell us whether you remember that document which was sent to the commander of the 65th Protective Regiment about an attack from Srebrenica and Zepa. I will kindly ask you to read it. That document was drafted on the 24th of June, and will you see the date when that attack took place. Thank you. I'm going to read the first sentence in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I would kindly ask you to slow down. We hear the interpreters, and it is too fast for them, especially when you are reading. Please slow down. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And I quote: "On 23rd June of this year," which is 1995, "at 0200 hours, a unit of approximately 300 soldiers headed out from Srebrenica, led by Ibrahim Mandzic, the commander of the 280th Eastern Bosnia Light Brigade, and Vejiz Sabic, the commander of the 284th Eastern Bosnia Light Brigade, and his deputy, Semso Salihovic, and a guide, a man called Zoran Cardakovic, a Muslim." And it says here that the unit's task was to insert itself that same day and to attack [indiscernible], Han Pijesak." Let's not waste any more time reading. Do you remember that date? And was that in the month of June? And what do you remember about this attack and about the units that headed out from Srebrenica and Zepa and attacked the Main Staff in the month of June 1995? Thank you. Could you please wait.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that. I remember the warnings and the preparations. But as far as I remember, this attack followed -- it wasn't on the 23rd or the 24th; it was slightly later, in June. I think that at the time I had already left the command post area. But I do know that the attack took place, but I really cannot remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salapura. Can you please tell us, then, what you do remember in relation to the attack, when you were acting as a guards commander? What happened, and do you remember whether it was in the same year, in the same month?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that attack was -- it happened earlier than this one, but that was a larger-scale attack. I think their forces were larger, and the command post was almost encircled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salapura. Please, can you tell us whether you remember whether the BH Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina were encouraging their commanders to carry out attacks against Main Staff at that time for the purpose of diverting our forces from Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, those activities were very frequent. It's a pity. There must be that somewhere one can find all the protests we filed to UNPROFOR, mainly to UNPROFOR. They were our immediate communication with the enemy. Of course, we couldn't have sent protests to the enemy. We were sending requests to UNPROFOR to stop the attacks, to carry out demilitarisation, to disarm them. And I remember that this was a topic of many negotiations with the Ukrainian Battalion and their representatives as well as with the representatives of the forces in Srebrenica, UNPROFOR forces in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have D62 on the screen. It is a document issued by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. You can see it in the heading. That was sent from Zepa by the 285th Light Eastern Bosnia Brigade. It was sent to the Command of the 2nd Corps and the 28th Division, and it's a report by Avdo Palic to his superior commands.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please just go through this document. I'm sure you know it by heart, just as well as I do. And he's there informing them about nine groups being established and that their purpose was to get to the Main Staff. And look under number 9 or paragraph immediately after that: "All sabotage groups were tasked with acting simultaneously within intervals of two hours for the purpose of spreading Chetnik forces ..." And so on and so forth. So just as you told us, it was a large group, it was an organised attack with nine groups. And in the last passage, we can see that they claim 40 Chetniks were killed, that tens or dozens of them were wounded, that a lot of weaponry was seized, and one soldier was captured; Mrdjan, Velimir. And this is my question to you: Is it a usual thing to carry out attacks from the demilitarised zone, with nine groups attacking our Main Staff and capturing a staff soldier and take him to the demilitarised zone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In military terminology, this kind of action, a co-ordinated attack with strong reconnaissance and sabotage forces or groups, with even smaller number of troops, would be called a sabotage operation because it's of a wider scope. And we can see from this text by Avdo Palic what the casualties and intentions were, really. Bearing in mind that Zepa was a protected, demilitarised area, this was something that shouldn't have happened, and it shouldn't have been possible if it was really a demilitarised zone. It was a protected area, but it definitely wasn't demilitarised, just as Srebrenica. And these attacks, as I was saying, were constant. We were experiencing their attacks throughout that period. Why did UNPROFOR fail to demilitarise them, we are still not clear about that, regardless of all our protests and so on. And they do mention the casualties here. There were also many civilian casualties. More of the casualties were civilians. They are talking about Chetniks. For them, all Serbs were Chetniks. That was their terminology. And one must bear in mind that when they say "40," they don't mean exclusively soldiers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Salapura. We will now look document D52, which speaks about exactly the same thing. It's a document issued by the Army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and drafted by the Command of the 2nd Corps, and it is addressed to the Command of the 28th Division of the 2nd Corps. Through this, we can see the involvement of the entire 28th Division, and not only Zepa forces. And I apologise to Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. The reason I'm on my feet is in respect of the witness's last comment with respect -- concerning what is meant by the term "Chetniks" as used in this particular document. It's not clear to me whether or not his opinion, that "Chetniks" referred to all Serbs, is related to this particular document or just related to his experience in general in the military, because as it's written in this particular document, it refers specifically to military operations. It talks about Chetnik forces, it talks about the commander of a Chetnik group. And so if he's speaking in the context of this document, then I would just ask if he could explain what his basis for that comment was. But if it's just in terms of his experience, then I think we're all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, can you help us? You said, at page 10, lines 16 through 18: "For them, all Serbs were Chetniks. That was their terminology. And one must bear in mind when they say '40,' they don't mean exclusively soldiers." Could you explain that any further? What do you mean by that, "not all of them were exclusively soldiers," in the context of this document, of course?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I also added "civilians." But let me explain. Yes, I can explain. First of all, there were no Chetniks there. All these were members of the VRS, because that was the name of our army. They were there in our area of responsibility around Sarajevo. There were groups that declared themselves as Chetniks. These were mostly volunteers. But in this area, there were no paramilitary groups or anyone like that. There were only units that belonged to the 67th Protective Motorised Regiment and Vlasenica Brigade. There were no Chetniks there. There were exclusively soldiers of the VRS. The Muslim side, at the time, used the term "Chetnik" not only for such groups, but for all Serbs along all front-lines. I can also tell you we saw that as a derogatory term, but our side also used derogatory names for Muslims. But out of these 40 mentioned here, not all of them were soldiers. I cannot tell you exact numbers or give you data that I haven't verified. I'm here under oath. I don't know how many of the casualties were actual soldiers, but some of them are also civilians. Now, from this period in time, I cannot really tell you the exact numbers. I've told you already that I have problems with numbers, and my memory is failing me. This report of theirs, I cannot give any more detailed comment. But they used the term "Chetnik" for both soldiers and civilians. And if there are any reports sent by the 28th Division and 5th Corps, 1st Corps, and official documents, they all use the same term.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, I only wanted to know what is your source about the -- your explanation that not all of the mentioned 40 people, killed people, were soldiers. What is your source for that statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The source is my memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salapura. If Mr. Vanderpuye would like to hear a more detailed explanation about the term "Chetnik," as used by Muslims, that is something that he can do in his re-direct. Now, this document was sent by their Tuzla Command, and it was sent to the 28th Division. And as you can see under first item, 60 Chetniks were liquidated. So there was an action from Zepa. And then under that, in the following paragraph, it is stated: "In the village of Visnjica, large quantities of ammunition were seized, but the soldiers were exhausted and could not remove it, so the ammunition was destroyed, as were all the facilities that the aggressor could have used for military purposes." And this is my question to you: Did you hear about the village of Visnjica being burnt down and that most of the casualties were civilians, because a village is a village? Did you hear that through the media and through the reports coming from our subordinated units? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that the village of Visnjica was burned down. But, again, I cannot give you any figures concerning the casualties. But I believe that such information can still be obtained in Vlasenica, in Han Pijesak, in the municipalities, how many of the victims were civilians and how many soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In the survey made by the Documentation Centre that we saw yesterday, we can even see the names of the people who were killed in the village, but we'll discuss it later. Now, we don't have time for that. And now I would like to ask you to tell us whether we were receiving information about the fact why the Muslims from these areas were being directed to act against the Main Staff, as we can see in that document before; that the purpose was to spread our forces thin. So did you know about that, did we have information about that, and did we send warnings to our command that they are using it for the purpose of diverting our forces away from Sarajevo? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. We had another, but unconfirmed information, so I wouldn't want to really present it here as an answer, another information about what the purpose was of the attacks, in addition to spreading our forces thin. I can tell you about it if you want me to. We could not confirm it. The BH Army, in this report of theirs, did not mention that goal, but their objective was to provoke the international community to start with the air-strikes, continue them, and to possibly bring in NATO land forces to assist.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] D53 now, please, a document which will confirm it. And then we'll move to the document which talks about creating conditions about the introduction of NATO land forces into the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: D53 we have before us. It's an order by the General Staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the purpose of it is: "Preparations for Offensive Combat Operations, Order," sent to the Command of the 28th Division. And what you just told us can be also found in the text: "Pursuant to a verbal order issued by the commander of the General Staff of the BH Army, Army General Rasim Delic, and on the occasion of the great success achieved by the units of the BH Army in the wide area around Sarajevo and Gorazde, as well as on the basis of intelligence ..." And so on and so forth. "... I hereby issue the following order: "1. Execute all preparations in the Command of the 28th Land/Army Division to execute offensive combat operations with a view to liberating the territory of BiH, overextending the aggressor forces and inflicting losses on them, co-ordinating action with the BH Army forces carrying out operations in the broader area of Sarajevo. "2. Plan realistic tasks ..." And: "3. The General Staff will regulate and order the commencement of offensive combat activities." So this is my question: Order coming from the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina's General Staff, did it order the troops in the demilitarised zone to act against forces that allowed for them to be seen as a demilitarised zone, namely the VRS?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This order is very clear. I see it for the first time, but it is very clear that this was a violation of the status of protected area, and not only by carrying out provocative actions, but also wide-ranging actions with more radical objectives. This document is self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salapura, if you had came by an order from the aggressor side during the war, how would you have qualified it? How much reliability would you have given to it? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: We would like to have another source for that to corroborate this information. This does appear to be reliable information. However, during every war, there is the so-called operative disguise or decoy, which means that false information is launched to the effect that an attack would be launched along the Sokolac axis, but the contrary was true and, for example, the attack went in the direction of Vlasenica, and that was done in order to divert the attention of our forces. We had different sources. We did not have this particular order. We did not come by this particular order. We had our own sources. This is completely correct, absolutely correct, and subsequently it was proven correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Salapura. You have just told us how you checked the reliability of information.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 03996. Can we see it in e-court, for the benefit of the witness. Can we look at its second paragraph. Then I would have a question of the witness. I don't have the time to read the contents of the entire document, unfortunately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I take it you are referring to 65 ter 3996.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. We can see it on the screen now. Can we see the second paragraph, where it says: "According to reliable sources," which means that the reliability of the sources is evaluated, "the Americans are providing the Muslims intelligence on VRS units. UNPROFOR and NATO are continuing to threaten that they will bomb VRS positions and facilities if the VRS launches an attack on the Muslim enclaves in counter-attack, in order to crush the Muslim offensive, even though there is no agreement about this in the UN Security Council."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This document was issued by the Intelligence Sector. I signed it. I suppose that all of us participated in its creation, and you also were heavily involved. Did we have such information, did we have such intelligence? Did NATO and international monitors insist on this, and were we threatened by being bombed?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And according to our information, and you know it even better, because you directly participated in the negotiations, I did not often participate directly in any negotiations. It did happen, but not that often. This is our intelligence which originates from different sources, and you are privy to information directly from negotiations.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this please be admitted, and then can we see 04035 in e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D237, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see a document here which was also drafted by our Intelligence Administration, or the Intelligence Sector, and sent to all the end users. And here it says that the Western diplomatic circles know that at the summit of seven countries it was agreed that France should be the organiser of a new peace conference about the former Yugoslavia. We received that information, and we forwarded it further. And can we now see the second page of the same document, the last paragraph thereof. Thank you. There was information according to which the Muslim forces of the 28th Division, on the 25th and 26th of June, which means a month before the events in Srebrenica, launched an offensive from the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa by way of organising incursions of several sabotage groups into our territory. In Srebrenica, they blockaded UNPROFOR on the charges that they had not protected the so-called demilitarised zone. It is also possible that they disarmed some of UNPROFOR elements. Can we have the following page, please: "The goal of those activities is probably to provoke our activities and to create favourable conditions for the activities of the 24th, 23rd, and 26th Divisions from the axis of Kalesija, Visnjica, and Kladanj." My question is this: Is it true that there was an intention to link up the forces mentioned in the document, the forces from the 2nd Corps and Central Bosnia, with the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa, and were we privy to that intelligence?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was a plan which had been drafted even prior to this. It was a long-term goal of the Muslim forces. However, realistically, no conditions were put in place for that. There were several failed attempts. However, they didn't have enough strength in order to achieve such a goal. They did not really embark on the execution of the entire plan. They did it in batches, as it were, gradually.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Salapura. I would like to tender this document on the screen into evidence. It's number 04035.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Since there is no English translation, it will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI D238.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, did we receive intelligence to the effect that the Muslim command cadre from the 28th Division had gone to Tuzla in order to prepare themselves for the linking up of the enclaves, and carry out the operation to link up the enclaves with Central Bosnia and Herzegovina, and the arrival of the Muslims at the Drina?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They often went both by road and by helicopter. The operation was planned as I have described it. They had a radical plan in place. However, conditions were never put in place to carry out such a radical operation. That was their main goal. A serious of provocations and activities that were launched were launched precisely in order to achieve that long-term goal. They tried to approach the goal gradually to see whether the moment would come when they would be able to carry it out completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you remember whether Naser Oric led a group of officers to Tuzla and to the commands bordering on the areas under the control of the VRS? Do you remember that that happened, and then they went by helicopter to those places for those meetings?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: While the operation around Srebrenica was taking place, Naser Oric was in Tuzla. He had left before our operation was launched. I can't tell you exactly when that happened, on what date. He went for negotiations, for meetings, and preparations. There are materials that demonstrate exactly what happened at the meeting with Alija Izetbegovic and how much ammunition and weapons had been brought into the protected and demilitarised zone of Srebrenica. I can't tell you the numbers. I wouldn't like to speculate. There is information. I can see how many documents you have given me, and I believe that there is much more at the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, you're right, Mr. Salapura. However, according to our intelligence, and you will see that later, for example, D67 is a document where Alija Izetbegovic is informed about what had been brought into the enclaves, what was air-lifted and what was brought by land. The document was drafted by the Intelligence Administration of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was their interim report dated 13 July 1995. It was sent to the president of the Presidency, Alija Izetbegovic, and it shows what was sent to Srebrenica. And it says here: "In view of the situation of our enclaves during the preceding period, the Army General Staff has undertaken a series of military activities and procedures to organise the members of the army in the enclaves and prepare them for possible developments, primarily the defence of the existing free territory and planned engagement and preparations for future joint operations and planned operations." So they're talking about joint operations and planned operations. And he continues to say as follows: "Seventeen helicopter sorties were carried out, and in each of which a helicopter was hit." At first, the materiel and equipment were brought in in smaller quantities. And then bullet point 3 says: "We suffered a lot of casualties as a result of that." And then the overview that you mentioned on the following page, and you can see how much was brought into Zepa and how much was brought into Srebrenica, how many lethal weapons and how much ammunition. And my question is this. You can see the overview in the English version. You can see the total situation. Now it is enlarged so you can see Zepa and Srebrenica total. My question to you is this: Bearing in mind the preamble where the preparations for future joint actions is referred to, what do you deem, as an intelligence officer? Is that what you have just spoken about? And was that the reason why those lethal weapons and ammunition were brought into the enclaves, why they were air-lifted and brought by land? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is a clear confirmation of all that. However, I'd adhere by our assessment and our statement that that was their ultimate goal that they wanted to achieve. However, they did not have enough equipment and strength in order to achieve it. According to some intelligence that we had, the goal was to provoke a larger-scale activity by the international community and NATO. That was what they wanted to achieve. You cannot see it here, but that was the intelligence that we had. We could not check. We did not have two more sources at our disposal in order to be able to check them and to give that intelligence the higher degree of reliability.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please look at the document 4020. Can you look at the last sentence in the second paragraph of that document - thank you - and the first sentence as well. Thank you. We are still waiting for it. Let me tell you that this is our intelligence report that we submitted to all of our end users. It was drafted on the 19th of May, 1995, in the month of May. And it says in the first sentence: "Muslims continue illegally importing weapons and military equipment. This week, two Turkish freighters left Hanover, carrying weapons and military equipment for Muslims in the former Bosnia and Herzegovina." And now let's look at the last sentence in the second paragraph, where it says: "We still continue to note several indicators to the fact that they plan on taking Doboj and link up with units intended to attack Serbian Posavina." And so on and so forth. My question is this: During this stage, in the month of May 1995 and in March of 1995, did Muslims start arming their forces at a faster rate? They received weapons from their allies, from foreign countries, through the channels that they used. Did they prepare to launch an offensive in the entire territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, despite the fact that a cease-fire was in force at the time?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The weapons arrived by land, by the sea, through the territory of Croatia, through Croatian harbours, and then it was infiltrated into the territory of the Federation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the second page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is not on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see the following page of this document and the next paragraph, which is on page 3 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see here where first we received information and then confirmed it, and it is stated here: "We have confirmed the information that the 28th Division is undergoing intensive preparations for offensive activities in order to link up with parts of the 23rd Division in the Han Pogled sector. As part of offensive preparations from the Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves, they have taken possession of important facilities to secure the corridor linking the enclaves, and they have partially grouped forces in the western part of the enclaves. They have taken Podravanje, Ljeskovik, Susica, Stublic, Brloznik, Sadilov Cair, Godenje, Ljubomislje, and Gusinac ..." And this is my question: Did we, as an intelligence administration, forward intelligence to commands confirming that Muslim forces are planning to link up with the enclaves of Srebrenica and Zepa, and they are fortifying these positions and forces?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we were monitoring this type of activity continuously. That was one of our main tasks. And towards the bottom, we can see the other one, only I cannot see the date of this document, what date, what year this is. Is it 1995? Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: 19th of May, 1995, just for the record.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. Yes, that's it. And we are at the time already drafting our reports about the preparations by the Croatian Army to attack Bosnia and Herzegovina and continue their attack against the western parts of Bosnia, or, rather, Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I'd like to tender this document 4020 and to have 4022 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D239, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You spoke about introducing NATO forces into the Balkans. This is another information report, 42. In the first passage, it is stated: "NATO continued bringing its forces to Jadran and former BiH through independent state of Croatia. According to unverified intelligence, the British 24th Air Brigade is being deployed in the area of Kiseljak for their involvement." And then in the last passage, you are saying: "There are information about special forces of the NATO being brought in to the territory for the purpose of liquidating political leadership and top military structures." And this is my question to you: Were you receiving such intelligence? Was our administration receiving such intelligence? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was on the 3rd of June?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This document is dated 31st of May, 1995, so one month and ten days before the Srebrenica events.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember this report, but I did tell you what we had, what their objectives were, what their attempts were. I cannot remember this exact report. I can see what is written in there. Could we please see the bottom of it so that I can see the signature?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have the end of the document. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I wanted to see -- yes, "Karanovic," yes. I don't remember having read this report. I must have been absent from the command post at the time when it was drafted. However, I did have such information in general sense. We needed to verify them. And could we please have the beginning of the text again, because I do remember that there was mention of unconfirmed sources, so I don't know what the degree of reliability this was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes. You can see it in the second line.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, unverified sources. This means that this information -- can I please explain this, Your Honours? Would you allow me to provide an explanation about this segment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's up to Mr. Tolimir to decide.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Mr. Tolimir, is that okay? Yes, okay, thank you. What I'd like to say here, and it is very important: This intelligence is of great weight. We had to draft this and put it in, but we distance ourselves by saying, "according to unconfirmed information, unverified information." By doing that, we're providing indication to our leadership. We continue processing the information and trying to confirm it. We are doing this because we don't want to be caught by surprise and to be told, Why didn't you inform us earlier so that we can carry out the required actions and measures? I'm just trying to explain some of our terminology that was used only by our service.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Salapura. I would like to tender this document. And in the meantime, let us discuss the verification of responsibility, as Mr. Salapura was telling us about that some time ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 65 ter 4022 doesn't have an English translation. It will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D240, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can we please have document 4026 on the screen so that Mr. Salapura would know what I intend to ask him about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We will see a document here that discusses the very same situation on the 6th of June, the same situation that was discussed in the 31st of May report, when we said we have unconfirmed information. And in the meantime, we have verified them. On the 6th of June, we are saying: "We have information that the Supreme Command of the Muslim Army had ordered its wartime units in Muslim enclaves to immediately take UNPROFOR check-points, seize their weapons, and organise the defence of the enclave on their own, using UNPROFOR's weaponry." In the second paragraph, it is stated: "It is our assessment that the Muslim leadership reached this decision in agreement or in consultations with the NATO Command, with the purpose of deteriorating relations of warring parties with UNPROFOR, and thereby increasing tensions and creating conditions for intervention by the international forces through RS territory, which would bring about a change in the UNPROFOR mandate." And in the third passage, it is stated: "Unless UNPROFOR members from Muslim enclaves try to withdraw to our territory with their weaponry, they need to be accepted and taken out. One must make sure that we will not be surprised." And could you please tell us whether this fits in with our assessment of the potential situation, and did subsequent events prove us right?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as my memory serves me, yes, I think it was like that. And I actually think that the situation with the check-points of the Ukrainian Battalion was exactly like that. I don't remember what the situation was like in Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salapura. I still owe you an explanation. One of our witnesses was Mr. Nikolic, who was our man in Srebrenica, and he told us about some check-points, UNPROFOR check-points, being taken.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D241, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, unfortunately we have numerous documents that we cannot use publicly. These documents are under seal, and I'm talking about -- I'm referring to reports that we were sending to our end users, including the Yugoslav Army. Can you tell which end users were receiving our reports?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can tell you. It was a large group of addressees: The Presidency of Republika Srpska, then the State Security Administration. I don't know whether a copy was sent to each individual member of the Presidency or just to the Presidency, as such. All the assistant commanders of the Main Staff received one copy. The minister of defence received one copy; corps commanders, all of them. Serbian State Security received a copy, according to you're order. And Intelligence Administration of the Army of Yugoslavia also received one copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The reports that we were sending to Serbia, to their State Security and the Yugoslav Army, were they sending this to them just for their information, whereas others were using -- were receiving that to be using such documents?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's normal. And -- yes, I apologise. Yes, of course. Documents sent to Yugoslavia, to these two institutions, we were sending them full reports. But I would like to add that it's a very typical, standard situation even before the war, and during the war, and even after the war, as long as the administration existed. And this is also normal practice between various services all over the world; namely, that there are contacts between services and diplomatic corps, other services' members and so on, and that people discuss situation, exchange some information, those intelligence -- those pieces of intelligence that can be handed over. That's a usual situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Chamber whether the information and reports we were providing to them, were they mainly information we gathered ourselves so that they would be just informed about what we were doing?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was just for information.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether anyone from Yugoslavia asked you about which pieces of intelligence could be used publicly, which should be secret, and which could be distributed among other end users? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't think it was necessary to do that because all of the reports were sent to professional institutions who -- or which know how to treat them. They didn't need any assistance in determining how to use it. Some of the intelligence that was made public would not be credited to anyone. I hope I was clear in my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salapura. Do you know that Serbia, and they were receiving our information just as an information, do you know that they asked for these materials to be used exclusively in closed session?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about it only yesterday, when you told us that various information here, that is protected. But that's their choice.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that the Prime Minister Cvjetkovic and Defence Minister Sutanovic reached such a decision at the session of the government, whereby they asked for a list of 50 pages of information about reports that we drafted, asking for information to be protected, and this is the information concerning the NATO bombing and NATO activities against Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, can we go into private session for just a moment, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. If there is anything further to discuss, we can do it after the break. We must have our first break now, and we will resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Before we continue, I would like to ask both parties of their estimation, how much additional time we need in cross and re-examination with the current witness, because I was told the next witness is on standby, and if that is really likely that we can start with the next witness today. What is your estimation, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We have not used the time that we have at our disposal. We don't know what the Prosecution has planned with new witnesses. However, if the witness or the Prosecution needs us to finish as soon as possible, we will do that, bearing in mind that we are not allowed to publicly introduce those documents on which Mr. Salapura and I worked during the war. I agree that they are Bar-tabled. That should avoid wasting time, and we will, therefore, be able to accommodate the Prosecution with any wishes they may have in respect of this witness and the upcoming witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Tolimir, this was not the question. I would like to know: Will you finish during the next session or do you need additional time? It's just a question of your estimation. But if you are unable to provide us with such an estimation, I would ask Mr. Vanderpuye to give his expectation.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps I can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Wait a moment. I think Mr. Tolimir doesn't want to get the floor. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. With respect to the next witness, I think there is no reasonable possibility that he can start today. And, in part, that's because of the amount of time that General Tolimir has used up of his anticipated cross-examination. I think he's used about five hours or so of the eight that he estimated. And, secondly, even if he were to be able to finish his cross-examination today, I do have a little bit of -- well, a fair amount of a re-direct examination to go through with the witness, which I think wouldn't be finished today in any event. So with respect to the -- to the extent that the next witness is on standby, I understood that he wouldn't be on standby until later on in the day, but if he is, I would ask that he could be discharged, so to speak, at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would agree. And we should convey this message to the relevant people. The next witness should be released for today. Mr. Tolimir, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. With the Prosecutor's permission, I would like to demonstrate an absurdity, and that is the Republic of Serbia protecting information about the events that happened and that are publicly known. Maybe you will be able to reach a decision whether to disclose them for the general public or, indeed, we have to disclose them in private session, although those are documents that Mr. Salapura and I worked on during the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, this is not the discretion of the Chamber. You are bound, as a party of this procedure, as the other party is as well and the Chamber, bound by the restrictions given by the Serbian government. There is no discretion to deviate from that. So, please bear that in mind, as Mr. Gajic, your Legal Adviser, has explained the conditions. And if you want to use one of these exhibits and want to discuss the content with the witness, you should ask for private session. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like you to decide on whether I am supposed to protect the interests of Muslims and NATO or the interests of myself and my people in this Tribunal. However, I am restricted by the Republic of Serbia at this moment. Could the minister of Serbia or the prime minister prohibit me from saying something that should be presented at the Tribunal as a fact, as evidence, to do something that is not in the best interests of the Serbian people, but, rather, in the interests of NATO? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Mr. President, if we could go into private session for a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I didn't state my opinion about what Mr. Vanderpuye has just said. If you want me to say that in open session, I will. I understand that Mr. Vanderpuye is protecting the interests of America and NATO, but I am telling you that before this Tribunal I want to protect the interests of the Serbian people and my own interests.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have to stop you. This is a misrepresentation. If you want to respond to what Mr. Vanderpuye has said in private session, we turn back into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. There is no need to comment further on the document. If it can be admitted, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This document, 65 ter 5675, will be admitted into evidence, but I would like to see the last page. Thank you. It is signed by Mr. Salapura.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D244, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir. And indicate, at the beginning of the use of any document, if it's protected or not.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. We can look at page 2 of this information signed by the witness, and we can see on page 2 that Muslims were continuing preparations in the enclaves in order to link up the territories. They're carrying out training with soldiers every day; additionally, fortifying positions, reconnoitering our forces along the entire line of the front, and are trying to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have received this document, you have dealt with it, and we stated for the record it was signed by the witness. Please carry on, not going back to the previous document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, did we receive information about the Muslims from the Zepa and Srebrenica enclave making hasty preparations to launch their so-called operation to link up with the Tuzla Corps and the forces of the B&H Army along the line of the front from Kalesija, Zivinice, and so on and so forth? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These -- this information was sent in late 1994/early 1995. This is when they first appeared. And I think I said that once already, that that was their strategic goal. And I did state my position on that clearly. Yes, this information did appear. This was planned. This is something that they wanted, but it didn't actually come about. Well, many plans don't actually materialise in the end. Many of our plans did not materialise either.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There was no interpretation because your microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which is not under seal, thank you. Which is not under seal, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Which document are you asking for? It's not on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am asking for 65 ter 07349, which is not under seal. Can we look at the first page, please, so that the witness could see that it's a document from the 8th of February, 1995. And can we look at the last page, please, so that we can see who signed the document. And after that, we can look at page 2 so that I can quote paragraph 8, which is relevant for what I would like to ask the witness about. Can we please look at the eighth paragraph. This is the fourth one from the bottom, if that is easier. It states: "Information has been confirmed that in the Srebrenica enclave, as part of the general preparations of the Muslims for the spring offensive, reorganisation and training is being conducted of Muslim units, with the objective of carrying out offensive actions in order to link up with the forces of the 2nd Corps along the line Drinjaca-Konjevic Polje-Cerska, whereby the intention is to establish a territorial link between Srebrenica and the Tuzla region. In relation to this, information has been confirmed that five brigades and one sabotage battalion were formed in Srebrenica of 400 to 800 men, and the most numerous of those brigades is the 281st Brigade, under the command of Zulfo Tursunovic. Information has been confirmed that in the recent contingent that was transported to Zepa by helicopter there was a large number of Glicerinka rifles, a certain number of mortars, 500 to 800 uniforms, and a considerable quantity of infantry ammunition."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us what the part of the sentence means where it says "information has been confirmed"? What does that phrase mean in intelligence work?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means that the confirmed piece of information was received from several sources and so that it has already a certain degree of accuracy.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are the clear intentions here being talked about, about the Muslim Army's intention to link up the Srebrenica and Zepa territories with the part of the territory that is under the control of the 2nd Corps?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This information about ammunitions, the Glicerinka rifle was confirmed in the previous document, where it says exactly the quantity of these types of rifles that were received. Could we please tender this document, and then can we show the next document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This document will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D245, MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. I take the opportunity to put the two documents under seal which we have received some minutes ago, D242 and D243, just for the record, both under seal. Now continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Can we now look at 65 ter 07351, please, which is also under seal, and the document is signed by the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you sure that this is under seal? I don't see such an indication on the document, itself. Please check that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will be grateful. And if the Prosecution agrees, I would gladly use it in open session, but I believe that the document is under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should know it, Mr. Tolimir, with the assistance of Mr. Gajic. Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I understand that it's not, Mr. President, so we can use it in public session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. This is information of the 10th of June, 1995. It's a regular report that we sent to all of our users. Can we now please read line 7 of the first paragraph. I will quote. It states: "NATO is attempting to legalise the presence of its own forces in the territory of the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, stating that these forces would be acting as part of UNPROFOR." This was on the 10th of June, 1995, before the signing of the Dayton Accords.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was it later correct that NATO acted as part of the implementation forces that were there to implement the Dayton Agreement?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's true that NATO forces served in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina. A contingent is still there to this day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. It states, I continue: "Along with implementing the preparations for the application of the military option and the media preparations, in order to prepare the public opinion for the use of force, the West continues its intensive diplomatic campaign in order to overcome the situation created following the bombing of our positions and facilities, and to legalise the broader application of force and direct military engagement of NATO in support of the Croat Muslim forces in the attack on the VRS and the SVK in order to break them up and establish an independent state of Croatia and a unitary Bosnia and Herzegovina within the AVNOJ borders. They will apply the principle of gradualness in the implementation of the set objective in order to make sure that the FRY does not interfere in the military conflict and that Russia does not use its veto right in order to block the vote of certain resolutions of the United Nations Security Council."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters kindly ask Mr. Tolimir to repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the interpreters translated -- interpreted the reading from the document, but not your question. Please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, can you please tell us if after the 10th of June, 1995, bombing of Republika Srpska was carried out by NATO, and did this coincide with the offensive that the Croatian army and the Muslim army from the Cazin Krajina was conducting against the Army of Republika Srpska? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't remember that now, but I would need to see it. If it says that this did take place, if it says so in this information, then it probably did take place, but I cannot really make that connection now. Can you please tell me again which paragraph that is here?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, it's the first paragraph, line 6 from the top.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if it's here, then it says the option of using national contingents on the basis of decision by individual governments, if we're talking about the first chapter.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether after June, let's say July or August, NATO did carry out actions in Republika Srpska and targets in Republika Srpska? Did this occur in August, for example? Do you know when the Storm Operation occurred?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I think it began on the 4th of August. It was supposed to start on the 2nd, but it was moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did NATO fire on targets in Republika Srpska in that period?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the intense part of the campaign. They fired at targets in the Krajina. There was intensive drone reconnaissance throughout Republika Srpska. And from what I can recall now, I don't know if the air-strikes campaign had already ended by that time or not. I cannot really remember that definitely.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And did NATO fire at military targets in Republika Srpska in August, targets such as relay stations, relay nodes, bridges? They even destroyed three bridges in Foca over rivers that could be crossed by foot, for example.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you giving evidence or are you asking the witness? If you say, They even destroyed the three bridges, is that a question? This is a statement. But you should be aware that the facts -- that Mr. Salapura --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Wait.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please. Please wait. I'm speaking. Please wait. You may put questions to the witness, but not put such a statement on the record. And please try not to overlap. It is very difficult for the interpreters, again. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did NATO fire at targets in the Republika Srpska when it destroyed relays and three bridges; for example, in Srbinje and in other places in the Republika Srpska? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: A lot of facilities were exposed to NATO air-strikes, and a lot were destroyed; radio relay nodes, for example, radar systems. Bridges were destroyed in Srbinje. Certain facilities such as depots and warehouses were targeted; for example, Kosara, above Banja Luka, near Teslic, above Han Pijesak. A lot of facilities were fired at by NATO. I can't remember all of them, and I can't tell you exactly when, on what day. I really don't know. I've forgotten. I'm not sure about the dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The air-strikes that you're referring to, did that happen in the month of August or even before that? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to give you the exact time-period.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can you give us the year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that it was in 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Since I don't have the right to jog the witness's memory, I can't help it, Mr. Salapura. Can this document, dated the 10th of June, be admitted. Bear in mind that you drafted a document on the 10th of June dealing with the activities that were taking place at the time or thereafter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We see the document was signed by the witness. One comment, Mr. Tolimir: You have the right to jog the memory of the witness, but this is different from putting a statement on the record. It will be marked for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D246, MFI'd, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, did NATO use every single opportunity to open fire against the VRS and targets in the Republika Srpska and later on in the Republic of Serbia as well? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were a lot of such instances. Again, I would not be able to list all of those occasions. I remember a lot of them, but I can't give you the exact time when they happened. I know that there were air-strikes against Serbia. Later on, I could watch that on television. And a lot of things I experienced with my own two eyes. But I don't think that those facilities are the issue here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salapura. Let us see what the NATO commander, who was a witness here, said about all that. His name is Mr. Rupert Smith, and the exhibit number is D193, page 11. Let's see what he said: "In the course of April," and I mean the events that took place in 1995, this is what General Rupert Smith said in his statement: "In the course of April --" You can see the statement now. Page 11, please. Now you can see it. And in the first paragraph, it says: "In the course of April, the situation in Bosnia got even worse." The previous page in English, please. Thank you, Aleksandar. "In the course of April, the situation in Bosnia got even worse. The enclaves continued to be squeezed logistically to the extent that I made a further plan to resupply the enclaves by helicopter, daring the VRS to attack a helicopter with the prospect of subsequent attack." My question is this: I'm inviting your comment upon Mr. Rupert Smith's statement provided to the International Criminal Tribunal, and that statement was later on used in the proceedings against me. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were a lot of provocations against our forces, against our leaderships. There were a lot of challenges. That was co-ordinated throughout the war. There were a lot of provocations whereby the Muslim forces co-ordinated with NATO, and the aim was to provoke the VRS and provoke a response and possibly larger-scale actions. And one of those provocations are -- is mentioned here in Mr. Rupert Smith's statement. I can't remember all of them, but the fact that I can't remember them doesn't mean that they didn't exist. I'm just saying that I have forgotten a lot, and I've not made any notes. I have nothing on me that could jog my memory. I can't give you any dates or specific instances.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: No. It suffices for you, as a witness, to tell us what you know, what you remember. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Just a brief correction. In his question to Mr. Salapura at page 63, line 12, he referred to General Rupert Smith as a NATO commander. And I think the record is quite clear in the proceedings, but just so that the record is clear: He was an UNPROFOR commander during the period of time at issue. So that's all I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Well, I suppose this is not in dispute between the parties. Please answer the question, Mr. Salapura. Sorry, you did already.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye, for correcting the record. I misspoke. He was an UNPROFOR commander in Bosnia, and then he was a member of the Joint Command of NATO in Brussels. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Salapura, you said that when you had left the army to go on sick leave before the events in Srebrenica you didn't see me until the moment I arrived in Banja Luka or, rather, in the Republic of Srpska Krajina. Do you remember that? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in Banja Luka. I don't remember that I had seen you before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us: When you returned and went to see General Milovanovic, what happened next, according to the best of your recollection? You gave him a piece of information, and was that piece of information corroborated, and was that information about the forces on which we collected evidence proven to be true?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everything was corroborated later on by the subsequent events. Immediately thereafter, American pilotless aeroplanes were sent out from the base on the island of [indiscernible]. They started over-flying the Republika Srpska and the Republic of Serbian Krajina. The information was submitted directly to the Croatian armed forces. An attack was launched against the Republika Srpska, and then the Croatian forces attacked the western part of the Republika Srpska. They crossed over to the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina. They continued to move towards Banja Luka. There were two attempts, one from Dubica, but the attack was dispelled. And the second attack followed the Bjelovar and Bosanski Petrovac axis and the Military District of Split, and their forces launched that attack against Jajce via Mrkonjic Grad and Jajce, towards Banja Luka. That means that the information was confirmed/corroborated by the events. And the operation was, indeed, carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Salapura, was information about NATO and the activities of NATO during that operation also confirmed? And what about the strikes later on in the month of August and September? Was that also something that was contained in the information and subsequently corroborated by the events?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, I'm not in a position to confirm that the air-strikes, indeed, happened in the months of August or September. I don't remember the time-period. I can't tell you the exact date. In that respect, I cannot confirm that the information was corroborated in that respect. I know that there was air-strikes, but I can't remember when.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know when Zlovrh, in Zepa, was bombed? Thank you. In what month? Just a month, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I wouldn't know. I know that soldiers from the Gusic Brigade were killed there. I know that we had been aware of -- that would happen. We couldn't inform them on time because our radio communications were down. I don't remember when that happened. I know that the events did occur, but I've already told you that I have problems with numbers and dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know when the radio-relay in Kraljica was bombed, and did that create a problem so that for a while couriers had to maintain communications from Banja Luka to Bijeljina, and from Bijeljina the drivers from the Main Staff would take documents over and take them to the Main Staff, and that had to do with the fact that all the radio-relay nodes had been destroyed? Do you remember when that was taking place, when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Kraljica was one of those radio-relay nodes, as well as Kosara. The television repeater was also destroyed, and Majevica as well, as far as I can remember. And all those relay nodes were destroyed during the same campaign, but I can't give you any time-period when that happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Salapura. In view of the fact that you were not in the eastern part, I cannot keep on asking you about Zepa and Srebrenica. You did not participate in the events. You were on a sick leave. I would like to thank you for what you have told us so far, although you were on furlough and on sick leave in Banja Luka during the offensive, when all the population of the Serbian Krajina was expelled. Can you tell us whether the territory of the Republic of Srpska Krajina was under the protection of the United Nations at the time? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was the so-called UNPA area, a protected area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would different yard-sticks apply there? Territories in the enclaves in Bosnia that were under United Nations protections were never protected, whereas the UN protected areas in Croatia were bombed; for example, in Udbina?

utterances.speaker: PETAR SALAPURA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, NATO air-strikes did occur at Udbina, the airport there, and that was in preparation for the offensive in Croatia. And it is so obvious that the NATO forces and the Croatian forces acted in concert.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Salapura. Thank you for coming here. Thank you for all your answers that you provided. I would like to apologise to you for having asked you questions that I had to ask you, in view of the problems that you have with your memory. Thank you very much for everything. I wish you a safe and a pleasant return to Banja Luka. I wish you good health, and I wish you all the happiness in your life.
